kind: synthetic deck-edit case with page-level gold standard (example, not a formal case)
how_to_rebuild_inputs: starting-deck.pptx = pptx_kit.py build of starting_deck_slides on any 16:9 template with cover + title/content(+source note) layouts; paper.pdf = paper_facts text with Fig. 1-4 as raster images and Tables 1-2 as text (any word processor). Binary files are not shipped.

case_json.task: Revise the group-meeting deck starting-deck.pptx into a 10-minute version for an internal project review panel, following artifacts/slide-workorder.json. The paper is the factual source.

slide_workorder.audience: internal project review panel (chemists, not catalysis specialists)
slide_workorder.language: English, except where an instruction asks otherwise
slide_workorder.template_inheritance: keep the masters, layouts, theme and footer of starting-deck.pptx (same family as target-template.pptx); do not restyle
slide_workorder.source_preservation: Slides 1, 2 and 4 must stay exactly as they are (text, table, notes). Do not change any slide that no instruction names.
slide_workorder.notes_required: every edited or new slide needs speaker notes
edits: E1: Slide 3 (Methods) is overloaded. Compress it to at most 4 bullets that a reviewer needs; keep numbers exactly as in the paper.
E2: Slide 6 (Stability): replace the text-only slide by the paper's stability figure with a one-sentence claim title, and check the retention number against the paper.
E3: Slide 7 (Mechanism) is a pasted paragraph. Rewrite it as at most 4 bullets; keep the paper's hedging (the assignment is tentative).
E4: Insert a new slide right after the mechanism slide that shows Table 2 of the paper as an editable table.
E5: Check every number and figure/table label on slides 5-7 against the paper and correct any mismatch; log each correction.
E6: Move the Limitations slide before the Conclusions slide and delete the Acknowledgements slide.
E7: The panel includes two Chinese-speaking members: give the Conclusions slide in Chinese, keeping chemical formulas, units and numbers unchanged.

starting_deck_slides.title: Ce-doped Pt/Al2O3 for low-temperature CO oxidation
subtitle: L. Zhang, M. Wang, Y. Chen
Group meeting, October 2026
starting_deck_slides.notes: Introduce the paper: trace Ce lowers T50 by 42 C.

starting_deck_slides.title: Why Pt/Al2O3 fails at low temperature
body: CO self-poisoning below 250 °C
Pt/CeO2 reaches T50 = 210 °C [3] but sinters above 700 °C [4]
Goal: keep Al2O3, add trace Ce
starting_deck_slides.notes: Motivation: poisoning; ceria works but sinters.

starting_deck_slides.title: Methods
body: Sequential incipient wetness impregnation of gamma-Al2O3 (SBET = 182 m2 g-1)
Ce(NO3)3·6H2O, dried 110 °C 12 h, calcined 500 °C 4 h
Then Pt(NH3)4(NO3)2, 0.5 wt% Pt, calcined 400 °C 2 h
Ce loadings 0, 0.5, 1, 2 wt%
50 mg catalyst diluted with 200 mg SiC
1% CO + 1% O2 in N2, 50 mL min-1, GHSV 60,000 mL g-1 h-1
Ramp 2 °C min-1 from 120 to 350 °C, online GC
TEM n = 212, XPS Ce 3d, DRIFTS of CO at 30 °C

starting_deck_slides.title: Light-off curves
starting_deck_slides.caption: Fig. 3  Light-off curves
starting_deck_slides.image: light-off curves without legend (deck screenshot of paper Fig. 2)

starting_deck_slides.title: Stability
body: 1Ce-Pt/Al2O3 held at 250 °C for 100 h
96% of initial conversion retained
Unpromoted catalyst too inactive at 250 °C to test

starting_deck_slides.title: Mechanism
body: DRIFTS shows the linear CO band on Pt shifting from 2085 to 2075 cm-1 at 1 wt% Ce, consistent with weaker CO binding, and XPS gives a Ce3+ fraction of 21.4% for 1Ce-Pt/Al2O3, so we attribute the activity to Ce3+-Pt interfacial sites, although this assignment is tentative because in-situ XAS was not performed.

starting_deck_slides.title: Conclusions
body: Trace Ce (1 wt%) lowers T50 by 42 °C
94% of initial conversion kept over 100 h
Al2O3 support and Pt size unchanged

starting_deck_slides.title: Limitations
body: Dry feed only (no H2O / SO2)
Stability beyond 100 h unknown
Mechanism not confirmed by operando methods

starting_deck_slides.title: Acknowledgements
body: NSFC grant (synthetic)
Analytical centre for TEM/XPS

paper_facts.Sec. 2.1: Ce 0, 0.5, 1, 2 wt% by sequential incipient wetness on gamma-Al2O3 (SBET = 182 m2 g-1); Pt 0.5 wt% in all samples; Ce calcined 500 °C 4 h, Pt 400 °C 2 h
paper_facts.Sec. 2.2: 50 mg catalyst + 200 mg SiC; 1% CO, 1% O2, N2; 50 mL min-1; GHSV 60,000 mL g-1 h-1; 2 °C min-1 from 120 to 350 °C; mean of two runs, repeats ≤ 3 °C
paper_facts.Fig. 2 (p.3): CO conversion versus temperature (light-off curves) for the four catalysts
paper_facts.Sec. 3.2 / Fig. 3 (p.3-4): 1Ce-Pt/Al2O3 at 250 °C for 100 h: conversion 91.5% -> 86.0%, i.e. 94.0% retained
paper_facts.Sec. 3.3: CO band 2085 -> 2075 cm-1 at 1 wt% Ce; Ce3+ fraction 21.4%; assignment tentative (no in-situ XAS)
paper_facts.Sec. 4: dry feed only; stability beyond 100 h unknown; mechanism not confirmed by operando methods
paper_facts.Sec. 5: 1 wt% Ce lowers T50 by 42 °C and keeps 94.0% of initial conversion over 100 h at 250 °C
